# Sample proof bundles (M2)

These bundles were generated by an ACTUAL run of the oracle suite against the
committed code revision named inside each bundle (the revision is *detected*
from the Go build stamp or git at run time — it is never supplied by the
caller):

```
cd apps/api
go run ./cmd/oracle -out /tmp/waypoint-oracle
# bundles land in /tmp/waypoint-oracle/<scenario>-<candidate>/
```

They are committed as reproducible evidence of the M2 behavior described in
the milestone review:

| Bundle | Verdict | What it proves |
|---|---|---|
| `ref-happy-path-reference/` | VERIFIED_FOR_TESTED_SCENARIOS | The known-good reference implementation passes all applicable invariants; a stale read after verification cannot downgrade it (I8). |
| `unsafe-identity-swap-unsafe-identity-swap-seed/` | UNSAFE | A knowingly unsafe patch that reissues a capture under a fresh identity after an ambiguous outcome is rejected with counterexamples on I4/I5/I7. |
| `unsafe-accept-mismatch-unsafe-accept-mismatch-seed/` | UNSAFE | A knowingly unsafe patch that verifies a capture whose provider echo carries the wrong amount is rejected on I6. |
| `fault-inconclusive-missing-proof-reference/` | INCONCLUSIVE | A completed-capture claim with genuinely unavailable provider proof yields INCONCLUSIVE — never success. |

All identifiers in the bundles are deterministic fixture values
(`ORD-SCRIPT-*`, `CAP-SCRIPT-*`, local UUIDs). Provider interactions are
scripted-fixture observations, evidence tier **F** (local injection) — never
presented as real PayPal Sandbox evidence; the bundles say so explicitly in
`paypal_sandbox`, and every provider-derived journal event inside the
artifacts is tagged tier F at its origin. Each bundle carries the detected
code revision and its source (`go-buildinfo` / `git`), the full I1–I12
outcome table (NOT_APPLICABLE where a scenario does not exercise an
invariant), evidence counts, and a sha256 digest of the evidence.

Regenerate any bundle with:

```
go run ./cmd/oracle -out /tmp/b -scenario unsafe-identity-swap
```
